meta.title: One bid: award all 10 units to Vendor A; approver rejects
gaps: Verify that the approver rejects the proposal with a remark.
Verify that no purchase order is created after rejection.
Verify that the buyer can start awarding again from Master QCS after rejection.
Verify that the awarded allocation specifically contains exactly 10 units, because no catalog step reads the allocated quantity on the awarding or proposal screen.
warnings: can only test part of this — no step for: Verify that the approver rejects the proposal with a remark.; Verify that no purchase order is created after rejection.; Verify that the buyer can start awarding again from Master QCS after rejection.; Verify that the awarded allocation specifically contains exactly 10 units, because no catalog step reads the allocated quantity on the awarding or proposal screen.

steps.note: Open the prepared closed RFQ directly on Master QCS.
Verify the single real vendor column is Vendor A.
Verify Vendor A's offered quantity from the prepared event data.
Verify Vendor A's bid rate from the prepared event data.
Verify the displayed line amount and total equal rate multiplied by quantity.
Open the awarding screen for the closed bid.
Allocate the available line to Vendor A.
Verify all line items and one vendor are selected for award.
Create the award proposal from the completed allocation.
Verify the proposal identifies Vendor A as the proposed vendor.
Verify the proposal shows the expected total amount when rendered.
Verify the proposal page exposes the expected proposal sections.
Fill mandatory proposal fields before submission.
Submit the completed proposal for approval.

args.need: sign in as the approver, open the submitted proposal, reject it with a remark, verify that no purchase order was created, and confirm the buyer can start awarding again from Master QCS

steps.note: Approver rejection and its downstream no-PO and re-awarding checks require another user session and are not expressible by catalog steps.
